hook: Tell what happened, explain how something works and weigh two options, all in one relaxed German conversation.
intro: The closing conversation of this module — and of this whole stage of the course — in your own AI assistant with voice on: telling something that happened to you and explaining why, describing how something works, and weighing two options. Copy the exercise in, say 'Los geht's', answer in full sentences; the score and corrections come at the end. The tutor listens for a story in the past with signposts, a passive when you describe a process, purposes with um … zu or damit, and at least one two-part connector (nicht nur … sondern auch, entweder … oder, zwar … aber). If you can hold this conversation, you can plan something with a friend, tell a story over dinner and argue your case in a discussion.
tips[0].title: Tell, explain, describe, weigh
tips[0].text: Story (Präteritum/Perfekt + zuerst/dann/plötzlich) → reason (weil / deshalb) → process (wird … gemacht) → options (entweder … oder / zwar … aber). Four moves; the tutor prompts each.
tips[0].check.why: To weigh two options, entweder pairs with oder; weder goes with noch and sowohl with als auch.
tips[0].visual.moves[0].label: Tell
tips[0].visual.moves[1].label: Explain
tips[0].visual.moves[2].label: Weigh
tips[1].title: Purpose with the right subject
tips[1].text: Ich fahre Rad, um fit zu bleiben (I – I). Ich fahre Rad, damit meine Kinder es auch tun (I – they). Pick um … zu or damit by counting subjects.
tips[1].check.why: Same subject (I get up, I catch the train) and a zu-infinitive at the end: um … zu.
tips[2].title: Close with a two-part connector
tips[2].text: Nicht nur …, sondern auch … as the last sentence of an answer sounds complete and confident.
tips[2].check.why: The pair is fixed: nicht nur … sondern auch.
remember[0]: Story, reason, process, options — four moves per topic.
exam: Planning, presenting and discussing are what the B1 exam asks of your speaking — this conversation rehearses all three.
